hand.name: The Hand
hand.blurb: Thirty years on this ground. Slow, hard to move, and not especially worried.

stats._dodgeNote: docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 5, the retune. Lever (a) in the doc's own order: 'roll back The Hand's batch-3 flat bumps toward batch 1's 160/0.9/0 dodge and see whether batch 4's cards now carry him.' A full rollback (160hp/0.9 regen/0 dodge) went too far the other way: hand/brawler (this file's home pilot, tools/balance.ts's default seed ladder) landed at 14/24 -- fine -- but hand/kite on tests/run.test.ts's OWN seed ladder (`1009*(i+1)`, not the balance tool's default) fell to 5/24, well under the >=12/24 'completes all 25 waves on most seeds' bar. Restoring dodge alone (160/0.9/15) still left kite at 11/24 on that ladder, one short. 165hp/1.4 regen/15 dodge -- roughly halfway back on hp and regen, dodge unchanged from batch 3 -- clears both: hand/brawler 12/24 default ladder (was 17/24, target 11-15), hand/kite 13/24 on run.test.ts's ladder (was passing before this batch touched anything, and still is), hand/brawler 17/32 vs hand/kite 12/32 on the 32-seed crossover ladder (brawl still clearly ahead, as the crossover test requires). Deaths on brawler spread w6-w19, not clustered. Dodge turns out to be the load-bearing half of batch 3's fix for a bot that never stands still (kite, wander) -- hp and regen matter more to brawler, and only needed pushing back up about a third of the way, not all the way, once batch 4's own cards existed to help carry the rest.

passive.desc: Standing still 1s grants +9% damage reduction per second to 45%. Resets on move.
passive._bracedNote: Braced was 6%/s to 30% and The Hand carried 140 hp and 0.8 regen. The upgrade-roster rebuild (docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 1) cut the stat share of the offer stream from 65% to 26%, and The Hand was the one build in the game whose survival was ENTIRELY stacked common maxHp and armour -- five Feed Sacks and five sets of Fence Staples is roughly +100 hp and +10 armour, and it was 79% cleared on the brawler pilot, the strongest thing in the game. With that flood gone he fell to 33% and stopped preferring to stand at all, which is his whole identity. Restored HERE, in the passive, which is where docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 4 was always going to put it: "Deep Rooted -- Braced caps at 45%, not 30%" is that batch's own card, and 45 is its own number. Measured, not guessed: at a fixed 140/0.8 the brawler went 8/24 -> 11/24 when drMax went 30 -> 45, and did not move again at 65 -- the pilot stops standing once six enemies are on it, so past the cap Braced has no more standing time to convert. drPerSec 6 -> 20 moved nothing either, for the same reason. 45 is where the lever runs out, and it is the number the design had already chosen.

ability.name: Dig In
ability.desc: Immovable, 70% damage reduction, ends in a 140px knockback pulse.

hand.cardPassive: Braced — standing still stacks damage reduction to 45%.
hand._flatNote: maxHp 140 -> 160 and hpRegen 0.8 -> 0.9 are the second half, and they are deliberately small. Braced alone restored the STANDING PREFERENCE (run.test.ts's "each class does better at its own game" passes on drMax 45 with the flat stats untouched) but not the raw clear rate, and "completes all 25 waves on most seeds" flies him KITING, where Braced never applies at all. Flat stats reliably favour the kiter over the brawler in this harness -- a kiter converts hp into runway, a brawler standing in a crowd takes damage that scales with the crowd -- so the flat half is kept to the minimum that clears the bar. hpRegen 2.5 was measured and is NOT the answer: kiting went to 14/24 and standing fell to 9/24, which is the gap reopening the wrong way round.

kid.name: The Kid
kid.blurb: Home from school for the summer. Only ever safe at speed; stopping is the mistake.

stats._hpNote: docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 5, the retune: maxHp 75 -> 65. The Kid was never a class this batch's numbers named as broken -- she was the one class that landed in the 11-15 target (kite, this file's home pilot) on its own, purely off the RNG-stream shift five new Field & Ledger cards cause by existing in the pool at all (SS7.8: the same seed draws a different run once the roster changes size). She measured 16/24 once the rest of the batch's item and class edits had settled, one over the target ceiling. Contact damage taken over a full clear is under 20 total either way -- she is almost never hit directly, dodge and speed do that work -- so the cut lands on the pool she still draws from every hazard tick and every hit that gets through anyway. 65hp clears 15/24, deaths spread w2-w12, not clustered on one wave.

passive.desc: +1% damage per 2% of max velocity, to +50%. Zero when standing.

ability.name: Bolt
ability.desc: Dash with i-frames, leaving a dust trail that blinds pursuers 2s.

kid.cardPassive: Momentum — up to +50% damage at full speed, nothing standing.

_abilityNote: All six classes now carry their own passive and their own ability; the four unlockables no longer borrow `braced`/`momentum` and `digIn`/`bolt`. Each owns a different axis of a system the game already had, because The Hand and The Kid between them had already taken the MOVEMENT axis and a third variation on standing-still-versus-running would have been another stat spread. Widow: attrition (damage arrives on a delay and killing cancels it). Veteran: spacing (damage is a function of range to the target). Agronomist: status (the burns, bleeds and slows she applies hit harder and last longer). Drifter: tempo (a kill streak that a single hit ends). Abilities dispatch on `a.id` in the `tryAbility`/`updateAbility` pair in world.ts and in `updatePassive`/`onKill`/`takeWound` in player.ts; an id with no branch is a button that silently does nothing, so add both halves together.
_animRowNote: `animRow` is read by NOTHING. It is a leftover from a plan to play a clip on the ability, and the clip names in The Hand's and The Kid's entries -- `dig` and `run` -- do not exist: the shared humanoid rig in art/sprites.json declares exactly two clips, `idle` and `walk`, and only those are packed (checked against the built atlas.json, not the design doc). The four unlockables name real clips so the field is at least honest where it is new; the two originals are left alone because their entries are not this change's to edit and nothing reads either value.

widow.name: The Widow
widow.blurb: Buried a husband and a harvest the same autumn. Nothing out here frightens her.

passive._note: Attrition, not mitigation. She takes the same total damage as anyone else; what changes is WHEN it reaches the health bar, and whether it gets there at all. Standing and fighting through a blow erases it. Turning and running pays all of it. hpRegen is 0.3 against the old 1.4 and maxHp 118 against a first pass at 130: Grit IS her sustain now, and it turned out to be worth a great deal more than the flat regen it replaced -- she measured 22/24 on the parity ladder, the strongest class in the game, before the body came back down. Read `_regenNote` at the bottom of this file for why a flat regen is worth so much here.
passive._immediateNote: docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 5, the retune's lever (c): `killEnemy`'s close is MULTIPLICATIVE against the outstanding wound (`wound -= wound * closePct/100`), so at a brawler's kill rate -- 4000+ over a clear -- the wound is closed almost as fast as it grows regardless of `killClosePct`; measured directly, cutting killClosePct 25 -> 10 (a bigger cut than Black Dress's own +15 bonus ever gave back) moved her clear rate 21/24 -> 20/24, one seed. Contact damage taken over a full clear sat under 200 total either way -- she was never losing the wound she banked, she was banking almost none of it. `immediatePct` is what actually controls how much of a blow reaches the health bar before the kill-closing pipeline ever touches it, and it is the number this batch moved: 55 -> 85. Measured together with the flat-stat trim below (95hp/1 armor was tried first and barely moved her either, for the same reason): 80hp/1 armor/0 regen with immediatePct 85 clears 14/24 (was 21/24 before this batch touched anything), deaths spread w11-w25 rather than piling on one wave. `desc` below is rewritten to match the shipped number.
passive.desc: 85% of a blow lands at once. The rest is a wound that bleeds off over 5s -- and every kill closes a quarter of what is left.

ability.name: Hold the Line
ability.desc: Plants a 160px ward for 4s. Enemies in it are slowed 45%, and every one that dies in it heals 4.

widow.cardPassive: Grit — damage arrives slowly, and killing cancels it.

vet.name: The Veteran
vet.blurb: Came home, took the back forty, and kept the habit of watching treelines.

passive._note: Spacing, which no other class cares about at all: The Hand and The Kid both ask how FAST you are moving and neither asks WHERE you are standing. It is per-target rather than per-tick -- the same shot is worth different amounts against two enemies at different ranges -- so it cannot live in the stat block or in passiveDamagePct, and joins the additive sum inside resolveDamage instead. The penalty is the point. Without it this is a flat damage bonus with extra steps.
passive._bandNote: The bands are tight against the player, not against the weapon, and that is measured rather than chosen. The whole weapon ring targets the NEAREST enemy (`findNearestEnemy` in world.ts), so a range-scaling passive is graded against the closest body on the field on almost every shot. The first pass used 220/110 and Overwatch was a tax: the near penalty applied continuously in any crowd and the far bonus could essentially never be earned, and the harness had him at 0/8 kiting and 13/24 spacing. 170/80 at -20% makes the penalty a contact-range punishment and the bonus something a standoff actually reaches: 16/24 spacing.
passive.desc: +40% damage past 170px, and -20% inside 80px. He is worth what the ground between you is worth.

ability.name: Claymore
ability.desc: Sets a mine. Arms in 0.8s, then blows on the first thing within 90px, or after 6s: 55 in a 150px ring, knockback and a 1.2s stun.

vet.cardPassive: Overwatch — paid for range, charged for contact.

agronomist.name: The Agronomist
agronomist.blurb: Sent out to test the soil. Stayed once she worked out what was in it.

stats._batch5Note: docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 5, the retune: UNTOUCHED. She was measured at 17-19/24 mid-batch, above the 11-15 target, but that reading was taken while `waveHpScalar` was still carrying lever (b)'s since-reverted steepening (see formulas.ts) and before the five new Field & Ledger items had settled the offer stream (SS7.8: a bigger pool is a different run off the same seed). With the curve back to its shipped value and the rest of the batch's content in place, she lands at 12/24 on her own -- no card in this file needed to move for her.

passive._note: Status and economy. She is the only class that makes an ELEMENT pick matter differently -- fire, acid and frost all get better in her hands, and frost gets better as crowd control rather than as damage, which is why the slow shares the multiplier and takes a cap. Applied where the payload leaves the projectile in World.applyHit, not inside applyBurn/applyBleed: those are also the entry points for the Chili Shot's death-spread, and boosting there would compound a status with itself every time it changed hands.
passive.desc: Burns, bleeds and slows she lands hit 70% harder and last 70% longer. Slows cap at 75%.

ability.name: Field Sample
ability.desc: Lobs a flask 190px. It leaves a 120px slick for 6s carrying whatever element she runs -- or a 50% slow if she runs none.

agronomist.cardPassive: Cultivar — everything she leaves behind bites harder.

drifter.name: The Drifter
drifter.blurb: Works a season, moves on. This season he did not get out in time.
drifter._statNote: This stat block moved a long way, and the reason is a measured PRE-EXISTING trap rather than anything the class rework did. On 24 seeds the OLD Drifter -- momentum, bolt, 70hp -- died on WAVE 2 in fourteen of them and cleared 1/24 kiting, 4/24 brawling, 2/24 spacing. He had been a trap pick since the density pass halved enemy HP and damage to buy BODIES, and nothing measured it because the parity test only ever ran The Hand and The Kid. Momentum was hiding it (+60% damage essentially for free, because a harness bot never stops moving); Hot Streak pays nothing until you are already killing, which exposed it completely.
drifter._weaponNote: `projectileCount: 3` is the fix, and it is aimed at the real fault, which was the STARTING WEAPON and not the class. At T1 the Harpoon Gun (`hookFurthest`) fires one shot at ONE enemy every 1.8s -- and at the FURTHEST enemy in range, so it does not even answer the thing about to touch you. Proved by swapping it: with every other number about him held still and the same 24 seeds, he cleared 4/24 holding the harpoon and 13/24 holding the Scattergun. Stat inflation had been tried first and did not work -- 95 hp, +45% attack speed and +15% damage moved 4/24 to 4/24, because no amount of body fixes a class that cannot clear wave 1. `hookFurthest` now reads `projectileCount`, a declared stat that until this change only the Scattergun's `stream` looked at, so he hooks FOUR at T1 and the harpoon is a wave-1 weapon. Nothing else in the game grants `projectileCount`, so no other build changes. At 88 hp he is still the second-smallest body in the game.
drifter._lifestealNote:
lifestealPct 1 is the last point of the fix and the single most sensitive number on this class. He was 11/24 on the parity ladder with none, and lifesteal is what a kill-streak class should be sustained by -- kills are already his engine, and a hit still ends the streak whatever it heals. It is worth watching: at 4% he went to 21/24 and at 2% to 20/24, so this stat is roughly five clears per point at his damage output. Anything that raises his damage raises his healing with it.

docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 5, the retune: three batches of new items later, 1% measured 16/24 -- above the 11-15 target, and the note above already flagged this stat as the one to watch. The curve is a cliff rather than a slope in this range: 0.5% fell to 8/24, 0.7-0.85% sat flat at 11/24 (the same 24 seeds resolve identically across that whole band -- not every value moves a result), and 0.95% is what actually cleared it, at 12/24 with deaths spread w3-w12. Re-measure this stat first, before anything else on this class, if the roster changes size again.

passive._note: Tempo. The Kid's Momentum asks how fast you are moving; this asks how fast you are KILLING, which is a different question with a different answer in the same fight. The whole streak expires together on a window from the last kill rather than a stack at a time -- decaying singly would put the ceiling out of reach at any honest kill rate -- and any hit at all, contact or hazard, takes all of it. That is the glass half of QUICK · GLASS · MEAN made mechanical instead of merely printed on the card.
passive.desc: Each kill is +5% damage and +2.5% speed, to 12. The streak lasts 4s past the last kill, and one hit ends all of it.

ability.name: Light Out
ability.desc: A 220px line straight through the crowd: 45 to everything crossed, shoved aside, 0.35s untouchable. Each kill on the way takes 1.5s off the cooldown.

drifter.cardPassive: Hot Streak — kills compound, and one hit ends them.

_cardNote: `tag`, `bars` and `cardPassive` are the class card's presentation, from the design's Home Screen mockup. Bars are 0-100 for the BODY/SPEED/REACH meters and are a READ of the class rather than a derivation from its stats -- Reach has no single stat behind it, and a computed bar would fight the design's intent every time balance moved.
_regenNote: hpRegen is an ABSOLUTE number and enemy contact damage was cut to 55% by the density pass in enemies.json, so every point of regen silently became almost twice as valuable. That is invisible in the class sheet and it broke `treats both classes comparably`: The Hand (regen 1.5, armour, and damage reduction to 30%) tanked a denser field comfortably while The Kid, whose only mitigation is avoidance, did not -- a 10-seed gap against a limit of 8. Raising The Kid's dodge was tried first and moved nothing, because the gap was never about avoidance. Regen is rescaled by the same 0.55 the damage was. Percentage defences -- armour, which is armor/(armor+k), and braced damage reduction -- are scale-free and deliberately untouched.
